To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The quality of care in ICUs in Europe is highly variable and the variation is not related to differences in patient severity or to differences in the number of beds per million population.

(a) the quality of care in the ICU is not uniform and varies widely among hospitals; (b) the quality of ICU care is not related to the size of the hospital or to the size of its ICU, but is related to the number of patients treated in the ICU, and (c) quality of care in ICU's is related to the quality of the nursing care.

(a) the use of the APACHE II score is associated with a significant increase in mortality in the ICU and (b) this increase is not related to the severity of illness, the quality of care, the number of ICU beds or the type of ICU.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: 1) the development of a comprehensive quality assessment tool which may be applied in different settings, 2) the identification of quality indicators which are sensitive to change in ICU practice and may be used for quality improvement, 3) the development and evaluation of a continuous quality improvement programme in the ICU.
the development of a quality improvement program in the ICU, based on the following elements: 1.

(1) the identification of quality indicators for ICU performance, (2) the development and testing of tools to assess ICU performance, (3) the evaluation of ICU performance and (4) the implementation of quality improvement strategies in the ICU.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

quality of care in the ICU should be defined by: - the quality and appropriateness of the care given; - the effectiveness of the care given (outcome); - the efficiency of the care given, and - the patient's and family's satisfaction with the care given.

quality of care should be defined as the degree to which health services for individuals and populations increase the likelihood of desired health outcomes and are consistent with current professional knowledge.

continuous improvement in the ICU is an ongoing process which requires a multidisciplinary team effort, a commitment from the top of the organization to the bottom and the active involvement of all members of the team.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quality of intensive therapy is not only determined by the quality of care but also by the quality of the patient.

the quality of ICU care is determined by: (a) the appropriateness of ICU admission; (b) the appropriatenesses of ICU treatment and the use of diagnostic procedures, including the use of organ support systems; and (c) the appropriatenes of the discharge decision.
we have shown that it is possible to improve the quality and safety of intensive care in a way that is sustainable over time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of care is a complex and multifaceted construct that requires multiple approaches to measure and improve.
we need to focus on the quality of care provided, not on the quantity of care provided, to improve outcomes in the critically ill patient.
the ICU is not a place to die, it is a place to live.
